explanation: Fisher expressly overrules Gollehon's two-step money-mandating test, but the footnote states that section was considered and decided by the full Federal Circuit en banc (citing South Corp.); bench limb fails.

Division 2 disapproves/overrules the quiet-enjoyment line including Albert Properties, but all fifteen Georgia Court of Appeals judges participated (whole court), so it was not a panel decision; bench limb fails.

Three-judge panel overruled Texas Trading, but relied on intervening Supreme Court doubt (Weltover) and circulated the opinion to all active judges without objection (mini-en banc); recognised exception present.

Fourth DCA panel receded from Hillman, but justified it by conflict with its own earlier Harrell decision and Florida Supreme Court practice/rule (Adams v. Powers, Rule 2.040); recognised grounds given. En banc rule 9.331 existed (own knowledge).

El Paso panel overruled its own Daylin, but because Daylin could not be reconciled with earlier binding Texas Supreme Court strict-compliance authority (McKanna, Uvalde) and its own earlier Fleming; contrary-to-earlier-precedent exception stated.
Second DCA receded from Allen, but eleven judges participated (en banc court) and the opinion relied on the intervening Florida Supreme Court decision in Burdick; bench and exception limbs fail.
First Circuit expressly overruled Aroostook's sovereignty/sovereign-immunity distinction, but did so in an opinion marked OPINION EN BANC by six judges; not a panel decision, so bench limb fails.
